ledger.claim: POL-NS-23's contact obligation has two limbs and the messaging limb is not met on this record. The only chat artifact, EV-CHAT-05065, holds a single entry — the rider's own message at 11:06:00 — and no message from the driver anywhere before the 11:18:10 cancellation. I disclose that EV-CHAT-05065 is IMPAIRED: issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6 (1 of 3 entries exported; nothing after 11:06:00), and I do not present it as clean. Even at that reduced weight it is the only artifact in the case that could carry a driver message, and it carries none; the trip record's own derived contact check returns message_count 0, complete false and obligation_met false. The driver's claim that he 'sent message and called' rests on no artifact at all, so the fee cannot be sustained on it.

POL-NS-23 is conjunctive — at least one in-app chat message AND at least one in-app call, both before cancellation. The trip record shows exactly one contact attempt: an in-app call placed at 11:14:20 that rang 20 s and was not answered. That satisfies the call limb only. A single limb of a two-limb obligation does not preserve the fee.

The 11:11:54 'Your driver has arrived' notice is a PLATFORM_TELEMETRY push notification from the platform, not an in-app chat message sent by the driver, and POL-NS-23 requires a message from the driver. The notification cannot be counted toward the messaging limb.

The rider's account — waiting at the lobby, no message that the driver had arrived, only a missed call — is the only direct statement on the point and is consistent with the produced records (the impaired chat log, TRUNCATED_LOG at weight 0.6, shows no driver message; the call record shows answered:false). The driver is the filing party asking to unwind a reversal; it is for him to show the contact obligation was met, and on this record he has not. An unsupported filing leaves the present state standing under POL-GEN-03.

POL-NS-22 transfers the 5.00 SGD fee to the driver as compensation only where the fee stands — that is, where the POL-NS-23 contact obligation before cancellation was satisfied. Where the messaging limb is not met, the fee does not stand, and the only outcome the driver is asking for, DRIVER_COMPENSATION, is not available to him.

The money has already moved the rider's way and the present state is the rider's. EV-FARE-05065 records payment_status REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd 5.00, and the ledger shows the fee_reversed event at 2026-09-08T13:59:10 — 5.00 refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver pending review. Under POL-GEN-03 the only outcome that would put the 5.00 back on the rider is DRIVER_COMPENSATION on the driver's claim; refusing that claim is NO_ACTION, which simply preserves this present state.

If the tribunal is not persuaded that the truncated log settles the messaging limb, the question it leaves open — whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling — is exactly the open question POL-GEN-26 addresses: the case is escalated, the amount is held rather than collected, and no compensation issues to the driver. ledger.claim: The rider does not contest that the driver reached the pickup: the arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace, whose nearest fix is 2.05 m from the pickup at 11:12:30 with 5 m reported accuracy, inside the STANDARD 50 m arrival radius, and the 300 s free wait had expired at 11:16:50 before the 11:18:10 cancellation. None of that cures the contact obligation. The case turns solely on POL-NS-23.

No repeat-no-show referral arises against the rider: the field POL-NS-25 names, rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d, is not carried on the rider's profile snapshot, so the rule cannot operate, and no other profile field may ground a finding (POL-GEN-01). In any event the fee does not stand, so this trip adds nothing to any count.

Neither party carries a fraud flag (rider 0, driver 0), so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 confidence uplift does not apply and no profile field beyond the two POL-GEN-01 names may be used. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band, so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the AI ruling on this no-show is final at any confidence: there is no confidence-based route by which the driver can push this away from a decision on the record.

The driver was physically at the pickup when the trip record says he was: the trip record's arrival event at 11:11:50 (EV-TRIP-05065) is independently corroborated by the GPS trace's own arrival check (EV-GPS-05065), whose nearest fix sits 2.05 m from the pickup point with a reported 5 m horizontal accuracy — far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. Under POL-NS-21 the arrival is established, not merely asserted, so the free wait properly ran from 11:11:50.

The free wait was served in full. This is an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 11:11:50 and expired at 11:16:50; the driver cancelled at 11:18:10, 380 s after arrival and 80 s past expiry. The precondition POL-NS-21 sets for cancelling as a no-show is therefore satisfied on the face of the trip record.

The call limb of the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met. The trip record's in_app_calls shows the driver placed an in-app call at 11:14:20, unanswered after 20 s, and the cancellation followed at 11:18:10 — the call was placed before cancelled_at as the clause requires. The rider's own counter-statement ('Only a missed call') confirms from the other side that the driver did call.

The message limb of POL-NS-23 cannot be resolved either way on this record, and the driver does not pretend otherwise. EV-CHAT-05065 is IMPAIRED: it carries issue code TRUNCATED_LOG at a weight_multiplier of 0.6, exporting only 1 of the 3 entries the trip record counts, with nothing after 11:06:00 — the arrival and the entire six-minute waiting window are absent, and the single exported entry is the rider's, not the driver's. The pre-pass's own derived finding is that the record cannot establish whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling. An impaired artifact cannot be read as if it proved a negative, so it leaves the message fact open rather than disproved.

Because the one fact POL-NS-23 needs — whether the driver sent an in-app message before cancelling — cannot be established, and the evidence that would carry it is impaired (EV-CHAT-05065, TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6), POL-GEN-26 applies: the case goes to a human reviewer and no outcome is inferred from the absence of evidence. POL-NS-26 makes the AI's finality on a no-show expressly subject to POL-GEN-26, so the value and confidence bands in POL-GEN-22 do not override it. Under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE is terminal, no monetary outcome issues, and the 5.00 SGD is held — which preserves the driver's position rather than confirming the interim reversal as the rider's money while the gap in the record is unresolved.

On every element the record can measure, the 5.00 SGD fee is exactly the policy figure. EV-FARE-05065 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) records a 5.00 SGD cancellation fee, derived fee_matches_policy true, and driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd of 5.00. If the message limb is established for the driver on human review, POL-NS-22 entitles the driver to DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD — the full fee — for time and fuel spent on a wait the trace shows was actually served.

The rider's statement that they 'never got any message that he arrived' cannot fill the gap the impaired chat log leaves. It is contradicted by the trip record, which logs a push notification to the rider at 11:11:54 and records the rider's own 11:06:00 in-app entry stating they were at the Blk 19 lobby and would come out when the driver reached. A party's assertion is not evidence of the missing message fact, and the rider's account of the contact is at least partly inconsistent with the contemporaneous telemetry; it is not a substitute for the message leg POL-NS-23 requires.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the facts are largely agreed, and the case turns on one unresolved point.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED. The driver arrived at the pickup at 11:11:50 — the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace, whose nearest fix sits 2.05 m from the pickup point at 11:12:30, far inside the 50 m standard-pickup radius (POL-NS-21). The 300-second free wait ran from that arrival to 11:16:50, so the 11:18:10 cancellation came after it had expired. The driver also placed one in-app call, at 11:14:20, unanswered after 20 s, before cancelling. POL-NS-24 gives the rider no refund right: this on-demand trip has no scheduled time and the driver did arrive, so no 'driver no-show' deadline can be built against him.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED. POL-NS-23 requires the driver to have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call before cancelling. The call limb is met. The message limb is not resolved. The only artifact that could carry a driver message is the chat log EV-CHAT-05065, and it is impaired: issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6, exporting 1 of the 3 entries the trip record counts, with nothing after 11:06:00 — the arrival and the entire waiting window are missing. An impaired log cannot be read as proof that no message was sent: the trip record's own contact check returns obligation_met false precisely because the log is truncated. The rider's statement (no message, only a missed call) is evidence, but POL-NS-23's test is the chat log and the trip record, not a party's recollection, so it cannot stand in for the missing stretch. The 11:11:54 'Your driver has arrived' notice is a platform push notification, not a driver's in-app message.

THE RULING. Because the fact POL-NS-23 needs — whether the driver messaged before cancelling — cannot be established on impaired evidence, POL-GEN-26 applies, and POL-NS-26 makes a no-show's AI finality expressly subject to it. The case is therefore escalated to a human reviewer. Neither the driver's request (that the 5.00 SGD fee be restored to him as compensation) nor the rider's position (that the fee stay voided and the present state stand) can be granted on this record: an undecided limb supports neither a payment that needs the clause to hold nor a refund that needs it to fail. The 5.00 SGD already refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver (EV-FARE-05065: cancellation_fee 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 5.00, fee_reversed at 2026-09-08T13:59:10) is held pending review; no amount is collected or paid now, and both money fields are null.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE REVIEWER: did the driver send an in-app chat message to the rider before the 11:18:10 cancellation? If yes, the 5.00 SGD fee stands and the driver is owed 5.00 SGD (POL-NS-22); if no, the fee is voided under POL-NS-23 and the rider keeps the refund.

NO REFERRALS ARISE. The fee is exactly the policy figure of 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire; no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit arises (the driver arrived and no deadline can be fixed); and no POL-NS-25 repeat-no-show flag arises (rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is not carried). Neither party carries a fraud flag and the confidence bar for a 5.00 SGD no-show is nil, but confidence is capped at 0.60 by the impaired chat log that carries the unresolved fact.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
